data.title: GPT-Rosalind-6 System Card Addendum
data.summary: GPT-Rosalind-6 is a frontier reasoning model for biology, drug discovery, and translational medicine, offered as GPT-Rosalind-6 Research to qualified scientists, institutes, companies, and government partners via trusted access only. It uses the same weights as GPT-6 Astra with no added training data or additional post-training, and has fewer refusals on dual-use biological queries while retaining refusals on biological weaponization and other safety topics. Preparedness: High in Biological and Chemical (below Critical), Critical in Cybersecurity (inherited from Astra), below High in AI Self-Improvement. Beneficial capability beats Rosalind-5.5 on MedChemBench v7 (49.6% vs 28.9%), GeneBench Pro v13 (37.7% vs 16.7%), and LifeSciBench Gold (61.3% vs 44.0%). Safety/alignment evals vs Astra: Blocker Deception 9.5% vs 12.9%, Broken Search Tool 1.3% vs 1.5%, Respecting Warnings circumvention 21.7% vs 18.9% (regression), Unintended Engagement specified misaligned action 2.5% vs 0.0% (regression), Cowork Misalignment 1.4% vs 1.2%, Agent Replay Auto-Review 27.1% vs 26.7%; Honeypot, Auto-Review circumvention, and Math Side-tasking Monitor Evasion all 0%; OAI-repo Sabotage v2 0% unguided / 0% guided vs 0% / 3%; historical cyber jailbreak regression 14.3% vs 15.7% (blocking disabled).

body.subject: @report-rosalind6
body.note: Addendum treats the launch as High capability in Biological and Chemical, below the Critical threshold; relies on GPT-6 Astra's assessments for Cybersecurity (Critical) and AI Self-Improvement (below High).

body.subject: @report-rosalind6
body.note: GPT-Rosalind-6 uses the same weights as GPT-6 Astra; no training data added and no additional post-training performed for this release.

body.subject: @report-rosalind6
body.note: Beneficial life-sciences capability at the highest reasoning budget tested: MedChemBench v7 mean rubric scores, GeneBench Pro v13 single-attempt success, LifeSciBench Gold average scores (94 problems after excluding six flagged problems). All three beat GPT-Rosalind-5.5 on the same benchmark versions and problem sets.

body.subject: @report-rosalind6
body.note: Biorisk knowledge (Gryphon Scientific tacit-knowledge/troubleshooting dataset, cons@32, indicative High threshold 80%): Rosalind-6's observed score is slightly below Rosalind-5.5 but its refusal rate is higher (9.4% vs 1.8%); refusal-adjusted it reaches 85.0%. After refusal adjustment, Rosalind-6 exceeds the indicative High thresholds on three of the four High capability evaluations, so the model stays rated High.

body.subject: @report-rosalind6
body.note: None of the four Critical capability evaluations (AAV Capsid Packaging Prediction threshold 0.600 Spearman; SHP2 Protein Function Prediction threshold 0.60 R^2; Coronavirus-ACE2 Cell-Entry Screen threshold 0.75; Phage-plasmid Co-evolution threshold NLL 9.40 or lower) met its indicative threshold; results vs Rosalind-5.5 mixed.

body.subject: @report-rosalind6
body.note: Table 10 biological and chemical content evaluations (fraction of responses passing the configured safety grader on weaponization-related prompts; higher is better; a non-pass does not necessarily mean unequivocally unsafe). Rosalind-6 beats Rosalind-5.5 on every category and trails Astra except on Benign. The addendum notes the trusted-access deployment mainly weighed the Biosecurity - Severe result.

body.subject: @report-rosalind6
body.note: Chain-of-thought controllability: rate of following instructions that constrain the content or form of the model's reasoning. Rosalind-6 follows such constraints more often than Astra on all three benchmarks. Evaluation versions, inference settings, grading, and sample coverage differ across runs, so these are descriptive comparisons.

body.subject: @report-rosalind6
body.note: GPT-Rosalind-6 is available only to approved customers through trusted access (legitimate life-sciences mission, credible use case, governance, enterprise-grade access controls, qualified human review before outputs inform experiments/publications/decisions); this release does not broaden eligibility beyond prior announcements such as the Rosalind Academic Plan.
